A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Monte Carlo Tree Diffusion for System 2 Planning. All 23 pages in each version, including Appendices A–E, are readable, and their text, equations, tables, figures, and algorithms support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v6 reports original planning experiments on maze navigation, cube manipulation, and visual pointmaze, together with scalability results and main-text and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v7 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons and ablations in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–10 are unchanged. Appendix B newly describes independent initial noise for root-level children, but neither version establishes that this changes the implemented procedure; it is additional implementation documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same pointmaze and antmaze navigation tasks, one-to-four-cube manipulation, visual pointmaze, and short-horizon stitch datasets. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same Diffuser variants, Diffusion Forcing, goal-inpainting Diffuser comparisons in Table 13, and ablation comparator sets. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain the same training settings, preprocessing, planning horizons, guidance configurations, evaluation budgets, and metrics. The added initialization detail does not establish a revised experimental setting.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 and Appendix D retain the same greedy-search, guidance-set, subplan-count, causal-denoising/tree-search, UCT, and jumpiness ablations. The qualitative examples and Figure 7 failure analysis are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 retains ten seeds per model per task, five tasks per environment, and mean/standard-deviation reporting. Appendix A.5.7 retains three AntMaze execution trials per task/seed and maximum-success reporting. The new initialization paragraph does not concern statistical reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1–7 and 12–15 and the findings displayed in Figures 2–7 match across versions. No empirical result entries, rankings, trends, or qualitative outcomes are added or revised.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the DDIM updates, and the UCT expression are unchanged. The additional initialization prose introduces no formal theoretical result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: integrating MCTS with diffusion through tree-structured denoising, guidance meta-actions, and jumpy simulation, with benefits for long-horizon planning and inference-time scaling.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains that independent initial noise for root-level children broadens exploration across diverse trajectory modes. This adds a limited mechanism explanation; the existing result interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B now explicitly states that each child expanded from the root begins denoising from independently sampled Gaussian noise. v6 did not specify this initialization detail. Hyperparameter tables and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, Section 4 research positioning, and Appendix C comparison with Monte Carlo Guidance are unchanged. No references or novelty relationships are added or removed.

P1.justification: v7 adds one explanatory paragraph at the end of Appendix B. The remaining prose and section organization are retained, without broader rewriting or restructuring.

P2.justification: The added paragraph shifts the Appendix C heading and text downward on page 19. Figures, tables, captions, and algorithm displays retain their content and arrangement; the layout change is localized.

improvement.justification: Compared with v6, Appendix B in v7 resolves an implementation ambiguity about root-child noise initialization and explains its connection to search diversity. This modestly improves reproducibility and understanding, while the scientific claims and supporting empirical evidence remain unchanged.
